operative_context: System must distinguish between different non-rentable states (deleted items, maintenance periods, manual restrictions, temporary unavailability) in availability semantics and query responses
Availability state semantics must separate operational validity (whether an item exists and is managed) from temporary unavailability (maintenance, manual blocks, active rentals)
Availability query API must clearly communicate the reason or category of unavailability to prevent user confusion about item recoverability
Item availability status must be immediately updated when rental lifecycle events or availability controls change
exceptions: Items marked Unavailable through status toggle cannot be rented
Manual availability restrictions take precedence over otherwise rentable time windows
Maintenance periods block rental activity and make items appear non-rentable during the maintenance window
Deleted items should have distinct lifecycle handling separate from temporary non-rentable states
conflicts_or_obsolete: Availability query results surface operationally invalid records using the same wording as temporarily blocked items, misleading users about recoverability (E5)
Implementation path uses existing non-rentable status handling for maintenance without confirming whether UI distinction is required (E6)
Earlier discussion suggested single fallback delay after rental events, but current availability rules do not support uniform timing assumptions (E2)
notes: R50 targets semantic separation of availability states to resolve ambiguity between operationally invalid items (deleted) and temporarily unavailable items (maintenance, manual blocks, active rentals). Primary evidence (E5, E6) confirms that current implementation conflates these categories in query responses, causing user confusion. E13 provides the baseline availability specification (TOOLCHAIN-CONF-AVAILABILITY-01) defining calculation, query, and restriction rules. E14 and E15 reference related requirements on query correctness and deleted-vs-unavailable ambiguity. The core operative rule is that availability semantics must distinguish state categories to enable accurate user communication about item recoverability. Gaps remain on deleted-item mapping, UI distinction requirements, and category-dependent timing details.
